---
title: "Web route families on Cloudflare"
description: "apps/web route families built as OpenNext Workers and served behind the gateway: family manifest, pruning, build inputs, environment names and rollback."
updatedAt: "2026-11-19"
audience: developers
---

`apps/web` stays one Next.js app on Vercel. Selected route families are also
built as their own Cloudflare Worker (`tuturuuu-web-<family>`) and served on
`tuturuuu.com` through the gateway's service bindings. Anything not owned by a
flagged family keeps going to Vercel. Gateway dispatch, header contract and
rollback are in [Gateway Worker](/build/devops/gateway-worker#web-route-families).

## Why one Worker per family

OpenNext named `functions` are not a multi-Worker mechanism: the Cloudflare
entrypoint dispatches only to the default server function. Each family is an
independent build of a route-pruned copy of the app, which keeps every Worker
under the 10 MiB gzip upload limit (CI budget 9.5 MiB).

## Files

| File | Purpose |
| --- | --- |
| `apps/web/cloudflare/opennext/families.json` | Family table: `id`, `worker`, `kind` (`api` or `pages`), `enabled`, `held` (why a declared family is not enabled), `localized` (paths match after the `[locale]` segment), `assetPrefix`, `wrangler`, `exact`, `prefix`, `exclude`, plus the global `deny` list. Enabled families must equal `webFamilies` in `apps/gateway/src/manifest.json`, in order; every app route entry belongs to at most one declared family (test-enforced). |
| `apps/web/cloudflare/opennext/prune.ts` | Deletes every app route entry (page, route, metadata route) the family does not own, except `api/build-info` (the build probe; the gateway routes it only to the family that owns it). Refuses held families. Dry run by default; `--apply` refuses unless `apps/web/.opennext-disposable-checkout` exists, and writes `prune-receipt.json`. |
| `scripts/ci/web-opennext-size.mjs` | Whole-upload gzip size gate over the `wrangler deploy --dry-run --outdir` output; fails above 9.5 MiB. |
| `scripts/ci/web-opennext-smoke.mjs` | Serves the built Worker locally with the production Host, no provider auth and all outbound requests refused; checks `/api/build-info` reports the commit, the emitted `deploymentId` is `web-<family>-<sha12>`, and the family probe paths answer as expected. |
| `scripts/ci/gateway-deploy-config.mjs` | Gateway deploy config: committed `apps/gateway/wrangler.jsonc` merged with the live Worker's variables and service bindings, plus the origins and flagged family bindings. |
| `apps/web/cloudflare/opennext/next-family-config.ts` | With `WEB_OPENNEXT_FAMILY` set: `deploymentId: web-<family>-<sha12>` (cross-family navigation becomes a hard navigation), `generateBuildId` = the full commit, `assetPrefix` for page families. Unset: no change to the Vercel build. |
| `apps/web/open-next.config.ts` | `defineCloudflareConfig({})`: no incremental cache, tag cache or queue for API families. |
| `apps/web/cloudflare/opennext/wrangler.<family>.jsonc` | Route-free Worker config (`workers_dev`/`preview_urls` false, `nodejs_compat`), secret names only. |
| `apps/web/cloudflare/opennext/<family>.env.json` | Every environment variable name the family reads, and the names that must stay unset. |

## Building a family (CI only)

The build runs in a disposable CI checkout at the exact commit, never on a
workstation:

```bash
bun install --frozen-lockfile
bun x --no-install turbo run build --filter='@tuturuuu/web^...' --concurrency=2
printf 'disposable checkout for an OpenNext family build\n' > apps/web/.opennext-disposable-checkout
bun run --cwd apps/web opennext:prune api-identity --apply
WEB_OPENNEXT_FAMILY=api-identity WEB_OPENNEXT_SHA=<sha> bun run --cwd apps/web build:opennext
```

`build:opennext` runs `opennextjs-cloudflare build` with
`cloudflare/opennext/wrangler.$WEB_OPENNEXT_FAMILY.jsonc`.

Toolchain: `@opennextjs/cloudflare@1.20.17` (an `apps/web` dev dependency)
with `patches/@opennextjs%2Fcloudflare@1.20.17.patch`, which runs Next's staged
render tasks in sequence on workerd when `cacheComponents` is on. Parley and
Lettin keep their patched 1.20.6.

## Deploying

`.github/workflows/web-opennext.yaml` runs on every `production` push that
touches `apps/web`, `apps/gateway`, `packages` or the lockfile, and on dispatch
from `production` (one `family`, and whether to deploy the gateway). Both
deploy jobs run only on `refs/heads/production`, in the `colab-production`
environment that holds the account deployment token, so the production
promotion is the human gate. The token is the environment secret
`WEB_OPENNEXT_CLOUDFLARE_API_TOKEN`, used only by this workflow, with Workers
Scripts edit on the Tuturuuu account; it creates the family Workers and
reads and versions `tuturuuu-gateway`:

1. **family** (one job per enabled family): exact-commit checkout, workspace
   package build, prune, family build, size gate, local smoke, then
   `wrangler deploy` of the route-free Worker with the commit in the version
   message. Public configuration comes from the `PRODUCTION_SUPABASE_URL` and
   `PRODUCTION_SUPABASE_PUBLISHABLE_KEY` repository variables, and
   `ROOT_WORKSPACE_ID` is the root workspace constant; the job passes no Worker
   secret.
2. **gateway**: captures the live gateway settings, checks that every family in
   the `GATEWAY_WEB_FAMILIES` variable has its Worker and every secret name its
   wrangler config requires, writes the deploy config, then
   `wrangler versions upload` and `versions deploy` at 100%. `WEB_ORIGIN` (unread
   by the gateway, kept for deploy parity) comes from the `GATEWAY_WEB_ORIGIN`
   variable and `MARKETING_ORIGIN` is
   `https://marketing.tuturuuu.com`. The deploy config requires both origins to
   match their live plain-text bindings exactly. It refuses any acceptance
   hostname or Vercel protection bypass setting in the committed config, live
   bindings, or deploy environment. The pre-write log shows family IDs and the
   presence of these settings without exposing origin or bypass values.

Turning a family on: set its Worker secrets (names in `<family>.env.json`),
mark it `"activated": true` in `families.json` in a reviewed commit, add its id
to `GATEWAY_WEB_FAMILIES`, and rerun the gateway job. The gateway deploy refuses
any flagged family that the committed table does not mark activated.

## public-docs

Activated (`"activated": true`): the first family served on `tuturuuu.com`
from Cloudflare. Owns `/changelog/**`, `/docs`, `/ui/**` and `/visualizations/**`, with or
without a locale prefix (`/docs` and `/ui/**` answer the same redirects as
Vercel). Client assets load from `/_f/public-docs/_next/**`, which the gateway
strips before the family sees it. The family requires no secrets: the changelog
reads published entries with the publishable-key client. Without an Upstash
store the proxy abuse guard logs `abuse-guard-store-missing` once per isolate.
Server actions use a per-build key, so an action posted from a page built by
another deployment fails closed.

## api-identity

Owns `/api/build-info`, `/api/health`, `/api/auth/me`, `/api/v1/workspaces`
(the collection, `limits` and `personal`), `/api/workspaces/invitations`,
`/api/v1/notifications/**`, `/api/v1/user/**` and `/api/v1/users/**`, except:

- `/api/v1/users/chatgpt` (Node file store),
- `/api/v1/users/me/{avatar,banner}/upload` (sharp image transform),
- `/api/v1/users/me/playgrounds/**` (devbox preview proxy),
- `/api/v1/users/me/{password,delete,email,identities}/**` (session-mutating;
  they move with the auth family).

The family defines no server actions, so it builds with a random per-build
action key in ordinary CI. `PLATFORM_LOG_DRAIN_DATABASE_URL` stays unset on the
Worker: `lib/infrastructure/log-drain.ts` would otherwise open a Postgres TCP
connection. `VERCEL`/`VERCEL_ENV` stay unset because they select Vercel
client-IP trust; the Worker sets `TRUSTED_PROXY=cloudflare` and
`TUTURUUU_DEPLOY_ENV=production`. The complete name list is in
`apps/web/cloudflare/opennext/api-identity.env.json`.

The API identity Worker binds `ABUSE_GUARD` to
`tuturuuu-abuse-guard/AbuseGuardEntrypoint` and requires
`ABUSE_GUARD_KEY_PEPPER`. It assigns `proxy`, `ratelimit` and `integrity` to
the service. That covers proxy IP blocks, trust and appeal lookups, route
limits and handler limits. The proxy applies its existing per-instance
limits during a guard outage. The guard's per-family budgets and durable
operator stop fence bound the service, including when requests retry.

Dispatch `web-opennext.yaml` on `main` with `api-identity-seal-sha` set to the
exact commit for a size check, original Worker smoke and restored Worker
smoke. The family stays held for routing. Before enabling it, verify hosted
guard health and state continuity for active IP blocks and trust writers.

The API identity build replaces the legacy Redis client with a module that
rejects initialization. The original and restored bundle checks reject imports
and embedded code from the real Redis client. Password login, OTP enrollment
and verification, and MFA setup and recovery routes remain with the auth
family. The shared proxy's required MFA check still verifies provider
credentials and account assurance through Supabase, returning 403 for
required MFA and 503 if assurance cannot be checked. Marked offline reads of
Calendar settings return 503 while the offline guard is unassigned. The
emitted smoke checks that response with offline protection enabled. Qualify
the offline guard before routing marked reads to this Worker if that client
flow is required.

Calendar settings, native-integrity challenge issuance and enrollment use the
same store. The integrity budget is zero by default, and the Worker refuses
valid integrity calls at zero before subject access. Rehearsal requires an
explicit share within the service cap. Each verified principal can spend up
to 5% of the family share per UTC day.

A single SQLite subject commits issuance, consumption, key ownership, counters,
revocation and provider reservations. During the first rehearsal, cap the
allocation at 8,000 weighted commands per UTC day. Each subject call costs at
least eight units, so this caps admitted subject calls at 1,000 per day. Use a
staged burst test to choose a peak rate with headroom for both the subject and
the shared control object. Track latency, overloads, and SQLite growth across
the 90-day enrollment retention window before raising the allocation. The
platform's per-object ceiling is 10 GB on Workers Paid and its request rate
soft limit is 1,000 per second. Consider sharding actor-scoped records if
measurements show a bottleneck, while preserving atomic global key ownership
and provider accounting.
[Cloudflare Durable Object limits](https://developers.cloudflare.com/durable-objects/platform/limits/) and
[architecture guidance](https://developers.cloudflare.com/durable-objects/best-practices/architecture-guidance/).

The provider budget also caps each actor and emits one daily warning at most.
The persistent operator stop is authenticated `POST /control/stop` on the
abuse-guard Worker. It closes every family, including integrity and new
provider reservations, until `POST /control/resume`. Requests admitted
before the stop can finish. For a provider-only configuration stop, set
`NATIVE_INTEGRITY_PROVIDER_ENABLED=false` on the Web service. SQLite parity
tests cover expiry, ownership and counter conflicts. Worker tests cover the
zero budget, per-principal quota, and operator stop and resume.

Move the three route groups together. Reconcile existing enrollments and
provider budget and stop state before the switch, and let outstanding legacy
challenges expire. Map an active legacy provider stop onto the Web provider
switch or the operator stop. A split issuer/verifier rollout can reject valid
proofs.

## Rollback

Roll the gateway back to the previous version printed by the gateway job
(`wrangler rollback <version-id> --name tuturuuu-gateway`). Removing a family
id from `GATEWAY_WEB_FAMILIES` sends its paths to the `web-rest` fallback. The
family Worker
has no routes, so leaving it deployed serves nothing.

Regression coverage: `apps/web/cloudflare/opennext/families.test.ts` (route
ownership, gateway parity, disposable-checkout guard, Next config gating) and
`apps/gateway/src/web-family.test.ts` (dispatch, deny list, header contract).

## Path ownership

Each served path has one owner. Alias collisions are rejected by the family
and gateway manifest tests. Rollback is one action (remove the family id or
roll the gateway version), including bare-query fallback paths through the
gateway.
